cards.title: Route-Specific Identifiability Assessment for Parent-Metabolite Models
cards.claim: Assess parent-metabolite model identifiability separately for each observation and route configuration. Metabolite volumes and absorbed or formed fractions can be confounded, but which combinations are identifiable depends on the equations, measured analytes, design and fixed assumptions. Evaluate fixed and random effects separately rather than assuming that fixing one volume or fraction solves every model.
conditions: Parent and metabolite structural/observation equations are explicitly defined.
IV and extravascular models are assessed using their actual parameter sets and data.
required_inputs: Parent and metabolite input, formation, elimination and observation equations.
Measured analytes, route, sampling design and proposed parameter values for local information analysis.
List of estimated/fixed parameters, random effects and covariance assumptions with their justification.
limitations: The cited example demonstrates a diagnostic procedure, not a universal parameter-fixing prescription.
Local information results do not by themselves establish global identifiability or predictive validity.
cards.downstream_use: Identify parameter combinations that the proposed data can support and justify simplification or additional measurements before fitting.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
